thumb.title: Bumrah 0. Akash Deep 5.
thumb.sub: How India bowled out New Zealand for 356

concept: One spell, two ends. The cover sets India's two lead seamers side by side: Bumrah's 26 wicketless overs sit in muted grey and Akash Deep's five lands in white underneath, so the contrast reads before the numbers do. Slide 2 is a wicket bar chart where one glowing bar (Akash Deep's 5) towers over the rest and Bumrah's row is a sliver, which is the whole story of New Zealand's 356 in one picture. Slides 3 and 4 are single giant numbers: Blundell's 89, the innings that made Akash Deep's work necessary, then India's 59 for 3 at tea, the swing back. The last slide sets up the deficit and the question. Cricket blue, type and charts only: no player photos, no logos.
caption:
Bumrah: 26 overs, no wicket. Akash Deep: five.

New Zealand resumed day 2 in Christchurch on 246 for 5 and were all out for 356. Akash Deep finished with 5 for 99 from 31.3 overs, his fifth wicket coming when Matt Henry edged to Rishabh Pant.

Tom Blundell made 89 from 211 balls before top-edging debutant Gurnoor Brar to Akash Deep at fine leg. Brar and Anshul Kamboj took two each. Jasprit Bumrah bowled 26 overs for 49 runs without a wicket.

Then New Zealand hit back. Yashasvi Jaiswal was bowled by Henry for a duck in the first over and Kyle Jamieson removed Devdutt Padikkal and Shubman Gill. India went to tea on 59 for 3, still 297 behind.

Wellington was a draw, so this Test decides the series.
